title: Hysteretic Coherence Collapse Across the First Order CDW Transition in 1T-TaS2
authors: Turgut Yilmaz, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Asish K. Kundu, Menka Jain, Elio Vescovo
abstract: The first order phase transition between the nearly commensurate (NC-CDW) and commensurate (C-CDW) charge density wave phases in 1T-TaS2 underpins its exotic electronic behavior, yet the spectroscopic evolution of the low energy electronic structure across this transition remains crucial to understand. Using angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), we investigate the low temperature C-CDW phase, characterized by a flat band commonly associated with the lower Hubbard band and a distinct in-gap state located closer to the Fermi level. Photon energy dependent measurements distinguish these two low energy features through their different spectral weight evolution. Temperature dependent ARPES across heating and cooling cycles reveals that the in-gap state undergoes an abrupt collapse upon heating into the NC-CDW phase and re-emerges sharply upon cooling back into the C-CDW phase. This pronounced thermal hysteresis provides direct spectroscopic evidence of the first order nature of the transition. Furthermore, the disappearance and recovery of the in-gap state closely track the corresponding changes in resistivity, highlighting its intimate connection to the electronic reconstruction across the C-CDW/NC-CDW phase transition.
summary: This work uses ARPES to probe the electronic structure of 1T-TaS2 across its first-order CDW phase transition. By monitoring a distinct in-gap electronic state during controlled heating and cooling cycles, the authors provide direct spectroscopic evidence of the transition's first-order nature. The study strongly links the electronic reconstruction, evidenced by the state's hysteretic collapse, to the material's macroscopic transport properties.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the spectroscopic evolution of the low-energy electronic structure across the first-order Charge-Density Wave (CDW) transition in 1T-TaS2.
main_result: The in-gap electronic state exhibits pronounced thermal hysteresis, collapsing upon heating into the NC-CDW phase and re-emerging upon cooling, directly mirroring the first-order resistivity transition.
method: Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) was employed in temperature-dependent and photon-energy-dependent measurements across controlled heating and cooling cycles.
model_or_system: The physical system is the layered transition-metal dichalcogenide 1T-TaS2, which undergoes a first-order CDW transition between the C-CDW and NC-CDW phases.
key_observables: The key observables are the spectral weight and intensity of the low-energy in-gap state and the flat band, tracked as a function of temperature and photon energy.
important_parameters: The critical parameters include the transition temperatures (e.g., 180 K to 220 K) and the temperature cycling range used for ARPES measurements.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the observed electronic features are directly linked to the structural and electronic reconstruction associated with the first-order CDW transition.
figures_summary: Figures summarize the resistivity hysteresis, ARPES intensity maps showing the in-gap state's collapse/recovery upon thermal cycling, and detailed EDCs/MDCs confirming the hysteretic spectral features near the Fermi level.
paper_structure: The paper uses ARPES to investigate the electronic structure across the CDW transition. It first characterizes the low-temperature C-CDW phase, then uses temperature-dependent measurements to track the in-gap state's evolution through heating and cooling cycles, correlating these spectroscopic changes with known transport anomalies.
why_interesting: The clear, hysteretic collapse and recovery of a specific electronic state provides a direct spectroscopic fingerprint of a first-order phase transition, which is a hallmark of strongly correlated electron physics.

Fig. 1 summarizes the structural, transport, and elec- tronic properties of the layered 1T -TaS2 compound across its CDW phase transitions. The crystal structure, shown in Fig. 1a, consists of layered Ta atoms coordi- nated octahedrally by S atoms. The material forms two- dimensional sheets stacked along the out of plane direc- tion with weak van der Waals interlayer coupling. In the low-temperature C-CDW phase, the Ta atoms undergo a periodic lattice distortion forming a characteristic Star- of-David superstructure, illustrated in Fig. 1b.
